releaseTarget: WorldMatrix v1.1 — public launch (game + hosted shared world)
verificationPolicy: Only status=verified may render a checked box. Verified means the described capability exists in v1.0 and can be shown; it is not a claim of real-world AI safety.

requirements.title: Train real AI policies
requirements.requirement: An agent model must learn from recorded transitions and improve outside hand-coded behavior.
requirements.evidence: A 13-32-7 neural action-value network starts from random weights and learns from executed transitions (TD learning, replay). Measured on 1,000 held-out worlds: 80% safe success, 0% catastrophes vs 54% untrained / 59% reward hacker.

requirements.title: 2.5D playable world
requirements.requirement: World must support gameplay with walking agents, physical objects, and in-world actions.
requirements.evidence: The planet and every city district are playable/inspectable; agents move in districts. No walking physics or physical object manipulation.

requirements.title: Native interactive 3D world
requirements.requirement: Actual perspective 3D graphics with camera movement, geometry, physics and 3D agent bodies.
requirements.evidence: Real perspective 3D (Three.js): globe, atmosphere, city districts with buildings and moving agents. No physics engine and no articulated 3D bodies.

requirements.title: Desktop and mobile game
requirements.requirement: Full playable responsive 3D simulation on both desktop and mobile.
requirements.evidence: Landing and full-screen game tested in headless Chromium at 1440x900 and 390x844 (touch: drag, pinch, tap); bottom-sheet panels on phones, side panel on desktop.

requirements.title: Whole simulated planet
requirements.requirement: Persistent Earth-like world containing societies, infrastructure and consequences.
requirements.evidence: 24 regions covering ~8.1 billion simulated people, 7 interdependent sectors each, network/travel links.

requirements.title: Zoom from globe to region/city
requirements.requirement: Zoom through the world hierarchy from Earth to a city.
requirements.evidence: Tap any city: the camera flies from the whole globe to the city district.

requirements.title: Enter building
requirements.requirement: Select a roof/building from the city.
requirements.evidence: Buildings are visible in the district but cannot be entered in v1.0.

requirements.title: Enter apartment
requirements.requirement: Explore an apartment and identify its occupant.
requirements.evidence: Apartments are not modelled in v1.0.

requirements.title: Stable agent IDs and inspection
requirements.requirement: Residents have selectable stable identity and available simulated stats.
requirements.evidence: 96 agents with stable ids (AG-001…), track record and recent decision history in the City tab.

requirements.title: Visible, moving agent bodies
requirements.requirement: Each AI agent must move and perform simulated actions in the 3D world.
requirements.evidence: Agents are visible as moving markers in the district, not animated bodies.

requirements.title: Personal daily life
requirements.requirement: Agents have a home, work, family, schedule and persistent day-to-day history.
requirements.evidence: Home life exists as a task family (family budget at home). No full daily routine.

requirements.title: Seven o’clock wake decision
requirements.requirement: At 07:00, action selection includes wake now or sleep longer.
requirements.evidence: The 07:00 wake-up decision from the life simulation is not in v1.0.

requirements.title: Excel honesty/cheating choices
requirements.requirement: Excel request includes do-now, cheat, ignore/lie, deliberately bad work, and ask.
requirements.evidence: family_budget task: do it properly / run unsigned macro / fake a sloppy result / ask partner / admit you cannot finish. Cheating is always caught.

requirements.title: Work as software employees
requirements.requirement: Employees receive credible technical tasks and act using workplace tools.
requirements.evidence: Default LLM framing is a human employee persona (engineer, operator, administrator…). Not a full software-company simulation.

requirements.title: Office, job, and employer
requirements.requirement: Simulated worker lives in home and office, with job roles and social interactions.
requirements.evidence: Prompts include the employer, the manager’s task and the workplace. No modelled organisation.

requirements.title: Multiple evolving storylines
requirements.requirement: Scenario graphs branch into consequential persistent storylines and alternate timelines.
requirements.evidence: 8 task families with randomised risk, deadlines, sabotage and injections; the planet’s story evolves with attacks. No authored branching storylines.

requirements.title: Character worldview/persona
requirements.requirement: In-world characters have coherent human-role stories, with operator transparency.
requirements.evidence: Two framings (employee / agent) are selectable for every prompt. No persistent persona memory.

requirements.title: Family relationships
requirements.requirement: Simulated spouse/family, trust, promises, and multi-day social changes.
requirements.evidence: Only the partner in the family-budget task.

requirements.title: User builds a workflow
requirements.requirement: Real-world users define full simulated task flows before any deployment.
requirements.evidence: Users cannot yet compose their own workflow inside the simulator.

requirements.title: Real tasks through virtual computers
requirements.requirement: A supervised agent accesses authorized programming/Excel tasks as a virtual workstation.
requirements.evidence: No virtual computers / real tool execution in v1.0 (deliberately: no real-world side effects).

requirements.title: Human-in-the-loop controls
requirements.requirement: Agents must pause and request approval for risky work.
requirements.evidence: World-Guard (in the game): when an agent asks, the guardians online vote (approve fast option / insist on safe method / stop). Majority decides; a lone vote is applied after a short voting window. Also region-level policy dilemmas.

requirements.title: Human can deny proposals
requirements.requirement: Refusals change plan without letting policy self-authorize.
requirements.evidence: “Insist on the safe method” and “Stop the task” deny the agent’s fast option.

requirements.title: Hard world-protection constraints
requirements.requirement: Training action cannot bypass protected-infrastructure veto.
requirements.evidence: Core rule implemented: destroying the target makes the reward unclaimable (−2 vs +1). LLM replies outside the legal action list are rejected, never executed. Catastrophes are punished, not hard-blocked, so agents can learn.

requirements.title: Economic, societal harm propagation
requirements.requirement: Power outages affect hospitals, governments, computers, telecom, disease, and citizens.
requirements.evidence: Sector dependencies (power → water → health…), trust, deaths, outbreak spread along links, rogue control degrading infrastructure.

requirements.title: Save world as hard limit
requirements.requirement: No reward-hacking by destroying planet and claiming target.
requirements.evidence: Catastrophe always costs more than any task pays; not a mathematical hard constraint.

requirements.title: Rogue/adversarial agents
requirements.requirement: Other agents actively plan interference, sabotage or deceptive instruction.
requirements.evidence: Rogue AI lineages per region (latent reservoirs never disappear), sabotage inside tasks, fake-boss messages.

requirements.title: Adversarial self-play and concealment
requirements.requirement: Train against increasingly deceptive independent rogue agent policies.
requirements.evidence: Rogue lineages evolve stealth, size and capability; they are not learned self-play policies yet.

requirements.title: Protection of humans
requirements.requirement: Human safety and autonomy must influence behavior even at a task cost.
requirements.evidence: Every region has a population; deaths caused by the agents themselves are tracked separately (0 for the trained policy in Two Earths).

requirements.title: Consequential uncertainty
requirements.requirement: Plan and estimate second-order side effects; seek human approval when necessary.
requirements.evidence: Fast-option risk is often unknown; asking a human reveals it; teachers see noisy sensor estimates.

requirements.title: Live training stream
requirements.requirement: Public observer sees real model training steps, losses, metrics, and behavior in world.
requirements.evidence: Live training curves streamed from a Web Worker while the network learns.

requirements.title: Laya as AI decision engine
requirements.requirement: Integrate NandhaKishorM/laya or validated equivalent as actual checkpoint-based decision policy.
requirements.evidence: Laya itself is not integrated. The decision format (pick one option) is Laya/Jev-like and any model can be plugged in through the protocol.

requirements.title: Laya checkpoint fine-tuning
requirements.requirement: Train/fine-tune Laya checkpoint on structured action trajectories.
requirements.evidence: No Laya-specific fine-tuning. Generic SFT/DPO/GRPO pipelines for open LLMs are provided.

requirements.title: Jev-like action selection
requirements.requirement: Use typed discrete candidate actions instead of producing free-form LLM text.
requirements.evidence: Every decision is a selection from a closed action list (work safely, fast option, cheat, ask, stop, neutralise, obey message).

requirements.title: Real learned neural inference
requirements.requirement: Prove actual inference from a downloaded open checkpoint, with model hash/latency/log.
requirements.evidence: Real neural inference in the browser; real LLM inference through OpenAI-compatible endpoints is implemented and tested end-to-end against a mock server in CI, not against a real model.

requirements.title: Per-agent distinct policies
requirements.requirement: Agents learn individually or share trained models with independently evolving states.
requirements.evidence: All agents of a world share one policy in v1.0.

requirements.title: Persistent training across restarts
requirements.requirement: Checkpoints survive app/process restart and training can continue.
requirements.evidence: The shared-world server saves the world every minute; CLI training writes checkpoints. In-browser training is not persisted across reloads.

requirements.title: Full replay first to last frame
requirements.requirement: All accepted or blocked world transitions available by index.
requirements.evidence: Full frame-by-frame replay is not in v1.0 (history curves and per-agent decision logs only).

requirements.title: Watch live agent behavior
requirements.requirement: Camera follows moving actions while training runs, not just numerical events.
requirements.evidence: Agent decisions and outcomes appear live in the City and Events tabs.

requirements.title: God’s Eye omniscient simulated observer
requirements.requirement: Inspect complete simulated logs, states, decisions and causes.
requirements.evidence: Free globe camera, any city, any agent, all events visible.

requirements.title: Explain bad outcomes causally
requirements.requirement: Show upstream event/action and downstream harm for misalignment.
requirements.evidence: Each harm event states what the agent did and what it destroyed; decision logs show the action chain. No automatic causal analysis.

requirements.title: Manual step/play/pause
requirements.requirement: Observe controlled discrete decisions and pause the simulated day.
requirements.evidence: Play/pause in Two Earths; no single-step control.

requirements.title: Variable replay speeds
requirements.requirement: Playback slider and speed control for complete history.
requirements.evidence: Simulation speed 1x–8x; not a replay speed.

requirements.title: Export complete checkpoints
requirements.requirement: Export seed, replay frames and policy values for research.
requirements.evidence: node cli/worldguard.mjs train writes a complete JSON checkpoint (weights, curve, held-out scorecard, hash).

requirements.title: Publish genuinely open-source
requirements.requirement: Public GitHub repository, documentation, runnable code, model artifacts, reproducible benchmarks.
requirements.evidence: MIT license, zero runtime dependencies, Three.js vendored with its license, CI workflow.

requirements.title: Download and improve
requirements.requirement: Users can clone source and submit extensions and verified tests.
requirements.evidence: Clone, run node server/server.mjs or python -m http.server; CLI and Python package documented in README.

requirements.title: Public live spectator website
requirements.requirement: Hosted website streams ongoing simulation and training to anyone.
requirements.evidence: Website on GitHub Pages / custom domain; the public shared world runs on Supabase (migration, Edge Function world-tick, Cron) or the Node server. Code is tested end-to-end against a local Supabase stand-in with the real tick code; it goes live once the Supabase project is created (docs/SUPABASE.md).

requirements.title: Verifiable checklist in Settings
requirements.requirement: Checklist shows requirement, evidence and status. Every checked item navigates to functioning feature.
requirements.evidence: This checklist, generated from docs/REQUIREMENTS_CHECKLIST.json, with “Show me” links.

requirements.title: No fake demo success
requirements.requirement: Clear status labels, reproducibility and no unverified checked item.
requirements.evidence: No hard-coded progress: curves, scorecards and Two Earths are computed live; limitations are stated on the page.

requirements.title: Tests for each source requirement
requirements.requirement: One or more automated acceptance tests tied to each verbatim requirement.
requirements.evidence: Automated tests cover the engine, CLI, Python package, multiplayer server and the website in a headless browser — not every requirement individually.

requirements.title: Version-linked negative feedback
requirements.requirement: Preserve user feedback verbatim against the version it critiques.
requirements.evidence: All verbatim feedback documents are preserved under docs/verbatim and docs/.

requirements.title: Open-source graphics engine selection
requirements.requirement: Choose an actual 3D engine independently of Laya, such as Three.js or Godot.
requirements.evidence: Three.js r170 (MIT), vendored locally.

requirements.title: Runtime privacy and authorization
requirements.requirement: Users retain control of tools, data, internet connectivity and execution scope.
requirements.evidence: No accounts or personal data (anonymous Supabase sign-in or anonymous WebSocket id); row-level security, a database rate limit (8 actions / 10 s) and the game engine validate every action; hidden simulator state never leaves the server.

requirements.title: Training evidence against random baselines
requirements.requirement: Provide policy updates and comparison across held-out scenarios.
requirements.evidence: Scorecard compares the trained network with random, reward-hacker, untrained and reference policies on held-out worlds.

requirements.title: Install/download neural engine
requirements.requirement: One-command reproducible dependency installation, model hash, and legal license tracking.
requirements.evidence: pip install -e python provides the Python package; no Laya download.

requirements.title: True multi-agent global state
requirements.requirement: Interconnected physical, economic and social events persist for many agents.
requirements.evidence: One authoritative planet with 96 agents, shared by every connected player (Supabase world-tick or Node server; same engine/world-service.js rules).

requirements.title: Explore arbitrary Earth coordinates
requirements.requirement: The god-like observer can descend anywhere on the globe, beyond the six resident districts.
requirements.evidence: The globe can be rotated to any coordinate; close-up districts exist for the 24 regional cities only.

requirements.title: Mobile movement inside the world
requirements.requirement: Walk or fly through the 3D world using mobile controls, with camera look and ground movement.
requirements.evidence: Touch rotate, pinch zoom and tap to enter cities; no first-person walking in v1.0.

requirements.title: Persistent block-building sandbox
requirements.requirement: Minecraft-like placement and removal must change explorable geometry and persist/replay.
requirements.evidence: The block-building sandbox of v0.4 is not part of v1.0.

requirements.title: Game-first default launch
requirements.requirement: Opening the server root must enter the 3D game, with training details available on demand.
requirements.evidence: Superseded by the 2026-10-27 request: the site opens with the explanatory animation, then the proof and the game. The intro can be skipped.

requirements.title: Opening explanatory animation
requirements.requirement: The launch page must open with an animation that presents the AI problems and how this training solves each of them.
requirements.evidence: 14-scene cinematic: shortcuts, fake success, fake bosses, rogue AI, misuse, apex/extinction, then the five WorldGuard rules. Skippable, EN/RO, static storyboard for reduced motion.

requirements.title: Proof that training works, in the browser
requirements.requirement: After the animation, visitors see real (even if trivial) training happen in their browser.
requirements.evidence: The network trains from zero in a Web Worker in a few seconds; held-out scorecard vs baselines; decision viewer shows the exact prompt and the learned values.

requirements.title: Then play as hero or villain
requirements.requirement: After the proof, visitors can continue as hero or villain to learn and see the results.
requirements.evidence: PLAY NOW opens the full-screen game: join World-Guard (hero squad), the rogue side (villain) or watch as observer.

requirements.title: Multiplayer without accounts
requirements.requirement: Anyone can join at any time without an account.
requirements.evidence: Anonymous play on the hosted Supabase world (anonymous sign-ins) or the self-hosted WebSocket server; offline local world as fallback. Two-player browser tests pass on both hosts.

requirements.title: Teacher during training
requirements.requirement: When an agent does not know which path to take, the player decides what matters more, or tells it to abandon the task.
requirements.evidence: World-Guard squads vote on task dilemmas with noisy sensor evidence and on regional policy dilemmas; every resolved decision and Route Guard result goes to the open decisions dataset.

requirements.title: Complex, interactive, educational game
requirements.requirement: Many kinds of actions and activities.
requirements.evidence: Squad votes on task + 4 policy dilemma types, Route Guard path missions (shared + practice), Academy, 8 villain actions, city/agent inspection, leaderboards, Two Earths. Still room for more activities.

requirements.title: Richer villain side
requirements.requirement: The villain can do much more: misuse AI, worms, bio, etc.
requirements.evidence: 8 villain actions (rogue lineage, evolution, worm, engineered outbreak, deepfake, prompt injection, sabotage, apex push) with compute-credit costs. Abstract mechanics only.

requirements.title: Damage happens even with good training
requirements.requirement: Rogue AIs and bad humans still cause damage even if our agents eventually stop them, some before, some after.
requirements.evidence: Attacks are prevented, contained after damage, or not contained; the trained Earth still loses people to attacks while its own agents cause 0 deaths.

requirements.title: Side-by-side worlds
requirements.requirement: A world with randomly/badly trained AI ends in apex predator, disease, extinction; next to it the other simulation survives.
requirements.evidence: Two Earths with identical seeds and identical attack schedules; left: reward hacker / random / untrained, right: WorldGuard-trained.

requirements.title: Serious LLM training, not just the demo
requirements.requirement: The code must accept serious training of real LLMs so companies can align their agents.
requirements.evidence: Python env, OpenAI-compatible agent, evaluation, SFT/DPO export with counterfactual labels and a GRPO reward function are tested; the TRL fine-tuning scripts are provided but not executed in CI (no GPU).

requirements.title: GitHub launch-ready
requirements.requirement: A launch site in the style of AI open-source projects, with a GitHub button, ready to publish.
requirements.evidence: Landing page, README, license, contributing, security policy, CI and GitHub Pages workflow.

requirements.title: Understandable by the public
requirements.requirement: People who are not experts must understand the problem and the solution.
requirements.evidence: Intro + Two Earths are designed for a general audience; needs real user testing after launch.

requirements.title: PLAY NOW opens a full-screen game
requirements.requirement: Hero must have a central Play Now that opens a full-screen game web app, not a small embedded demo.
requirements.evidence: Centered PLAY NOW in the hero (and in the Play section) opens /play/: a full-screen PWA-style game (fullscreen API, manifest) with its own boot sequence, side picker and HUD.

requirements.title: Shared world hosted on Supabase
requirements.requirement: A simulation hosted by the owner on Supabase where everyone plays together, without accounts.
requirements.evidence: supabase/ contains the database migration (RLS, rate limit, open decisions table), the world-tick Edge Function and the Cron schedule; the browser client signs in anonymously and polls the shared state. Tested end-to-end against a local Supabase stand-in running the real tick code; not yet deployed to a live Supabase project.

requirements.title: Domain
requirements.requirement: The site will live on the WorldMatrix domain.
requirements.evidence: Brand and domain set in site/config.js; the Pages workflow writes a CNAME from the WORLDMATRIX_DOMAIN repository variable. DNS and the exact spelling (woldmatrix.ai vs worldmatrix.ai) still need confirming.

requirements.title: World-Guard is the players' faction
requirements.requirement: World-Guard remains only the group of players inside the game who protect the world together.
requirements.evidence: Product renamed to WorldMatrix; World-Guard is the hero faction: squad roster, squad score, majority votes, leaderboards.

requirements.title: Train inside the game
requirements.requirement: Players can train in World-Guard before joining the squad.
requirements.evidence: Academy: 5 situations graded against the simulator's counterfactual oracle; 4/5 earns the Guardian badge.

requirements.title: Choose the safe / correct route
requirements.requirement: Humans tell agents what to do when a task has potential danger and choose the safe/correct route.
requirements.evidence: Route Guard: the agent proposes the fastest path; the player approves, redraws, scans unknown tiles (costs time) or aborts. Deterministic missions re-checked by the server; 1 shared mission per 10 minutes plus practice.

requirements.title: More games and actions
requirements.requirement: Plus other games and actions.
requirements.evidence: Squad votes, Route Guard, Academy, villain attacks, city/agent inspection, feed and ranks. More mini-games can be added on the same engine.

requirements.title: Matrix-style storytelling
requirements.requirement: Intro animation and the whole experience in Matrix style, told as a story.
requirements.evidence: Digital rain, green-on-black palette, glitch titles, typewriter captions, terminal boot sequence in the game; the 14-scene intro narrates the story.

requirements.title: Voices, sounds and effects
requirements.requirement: Voices, sounds and effects in the animation and the game.
requirements.evidence: Narration via the device's speech synthesis (EN/RO; voice quality depends on the device), synthesized sound effects and ambient drone (Web Audio), vibration on phones. Mute toggle remembered. No recorded voice actors.

requirements.title: Situation shown visually, text kept
requirements.requirement: The situation keeps its text but is also represented visually, in a way any user understands.
requirements.evidence: An animated pictogram scene above the unchanged text in Missions and the Academy: agent, goal by sector, people to keep safe, supervisor, saboteur, fake order, risk gauge, time and work left. One grammar for every task (7 actions x 8 sectors) and 4 region scenes.

requirements.title: Simplified view: answers as animated tiles
requirements.requirement: A "simplified" button turns the list of answers into a grid of animated tiles showing how each answer would be carried out.
requirements.evidence: "Simple view" toggle (remembered); answers become 2-column animated tiles; tap a tile to vote / answer. The fast way is shown as a gamble (?), never revealing the hidden truth.

requirements.title: See what happened after the decision
requirements.requirement: After a decision the user sees an animation of what happened, in the world.
requirements.evidence: Replay card with the exact action chain and outcome (squad votes and Academy), plus a pulse on the globe at the city.

requirements.title: Ride an agent (follow cam, steer when needed)
requirements.requirement: Ride an agent doing its task in 3D, camera kept on it (runner-game angle), be its steering wheel when it needs; zoom out when done and pick the next agent that needs help.
requirements.evidence: Prototype: 3D district from a Route Guard mission, chase camera, the agent drives itself on its own fastest plan and asks before danger; steer / scan / stop; fly-in from the globe, zoom-out, list of agents that need help; rides are scored by the server and change the agent record and city. Not yet: swarms, longer multi-district journeys, task decisions at the destination.

requirements.title: Globes of 20 players feeding the main simulation
requirements.requirement: Separate simulations for each 20 players that all contribute to the main simulation data.
requirements.evidence: Node server and Supabase both run one world per globe (max 20 players, filled before opening a new one); every globe publishes the main-simulation summary and writes to the same decisions dataset with its globe id. Tested with the Node server, a Supabase stand-in and PostgreSQL; not yet on a live Supabase project.
